tasks.short: Read committee papers, take part in committee meetings on institutional policies and academic issues, write the lecturer's part of the advice, and track actions.

steps.what: Lecturer reads committee papers sent by e-mail
Lecturer serves on academic or administrative committees in meetings
Lecturer writes the lecturer's part of the committee advice
Lecturer tracks committee actions by e-mail

tasks.design: Committee papers sit in a meeting portal ({DOCS}) per agenda item with the current version and earlier decisions, so the lecturer does not sort e-mail attachments. Advice uses the committee's template. Actions are an action list in the same portal with owners and due dates. Deliberating and deciding stay with the committee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Papers came as e-mail attachments in several versions and actions were lost in mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting portals hold papers per agenda item and action lists.
tasks.still_hard: Late papers still arrive by e-mail.

evidence.claim: Meeting portals can hold papers per agenda item, decision history and action lists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the committee agenda to actions tracked; policy implementation is outside.
Input contract: the secretary uploads papers; fallback is e-mail.
The secretary's time does not change.
research_questions: Do committee actions close on time more often?

incremental.description: Lecturer updates own actions in the portal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one small committee; high: several committees with long papers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find funding calls, plan the project with partners, write the grant proposal, build the budget, check the proposal with partners and the grants office, and submit it.

steps.what: Lecturer searches funders' websites for calls
Lecturer plans the project with partners
Lecturer writes grant proposals to procure external research funding

loop.input: The project plan, the call text and the lecturer's own publications.
loop.output: Draft proposal sections in the funder's format.
loop.check: Code checks every assessment criterion is addressed, sections are within the length limits, and every citation resolves by DOI; the lecturer rewrites and approves.
loop.stop: Up to two redrafts per section; then the lecturer writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each call asks different questions; a template does not argue the case.

steps.what: Lecturer builds the budget in a spreadsheet
Lecturer checks the final proposal with partners and the grants office
Lecturer submits the proposal on the funder's portal

tasks.design: Call alerts from funders and the grants office replace browsing funders' sites. A bounded step on the university's own platform drafts proposal sections from the project plan, the call text and the lecturer's publications; code checks criteria coverage, length limits and that every citation resolves, and the lecturer rewrites. The grants office's budget template holds standard rates. Planning with partners and submission stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proposals were written from scratch and budgets built by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: University platforms draft text; code checks citations and criteria.
tasks.still_hard: Funders ban hidden prompts and reviewers may not use AI, so the text must stand on its own.
tasks.altitude: The lecturer rewrites drafts instead of writing from scratch.

evidence.claim: NWO bans hidden AI prompts in grant applications; referees may not use generative AI.
Language models can draft proposal sections; code can check criteria, length and DOIs.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research idea to the proposal submitted; the funder's decision is outside.
Input contract: publications in the university repository; fallback is writing from scratch.
No confidential partner data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much drafted text survives the rewrite?

approvals.approved_version: The proposal as checked with partners and the grants office in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new topics; high: resubmissions of earlier proposals.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet government and educational agencies, exchange documents with them, report back to the faculty, and keep contacts and agreements.

steps.what: Lecturer serves as a liaison in meetings with governmental and educational agencies
Lecturer exchanges documents with agencies by e-mail
Lecturer reports back to the faculty
Lecturer keeps contacts and agreements in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Documents with each agency are exchanged in a shared project space with versions, instead of e-mail attachments. Contacts, meetings and agreements are kept in the university's relations system ({CRM}), so colleagues can see them. Faculty reports use a short template. Meeting agencies and building relations stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents travelled by e-mail and contacts sat in a personal spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared project spaces and relations systems are standard in universities.
tasks.still_hard: Agencies have their own rules on shared spaces.
tasks.human_edge: Earning an agency's trust for a joint project.

evidence.claim: Shared project spaces and relations systems can hold documents, contacts and agreements.

assumptions: Boundary: from the liaison topic to contacts kept; formal contracts are outside.
Input contract: agencies accept the shared space; fallback is e-mail.
research_questions: Do colleagues find existing contacts before reaching out?

incremental.description: Lecturer logs meetings in the relations system.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one agency; high: many agencies and documents.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange in-service seminars with schools, prepare materials, give seminars to teachers, and collect feedback and issue certificates.

steps.what: Lecturer arranges in-service seminars with schools by e-mail
Lecturer prepares seminar activities and materials
Lecturer advises and instructs teachers employed in school systems
Lecturer collects feedback and issues attendance certificates by hand

tasks.design: Schools book seminars on a request form with topic, group size and dates, and teachers enrol in the learning environment ({LMS}), so arrangements are not made by e-mail. Seminar materials come from a library of earlier seminars that the lecturer adapts. Feedback is collected on a short online form and certificates are generated from the attendance list. Advising and instructing teachers stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Seminars were arranged by e-mail, materials remade and certificates written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking forms, enrolment and certificate generation run in learning environments.
tasks.still_hard: Schools change dates at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Showing teachers a classroom technique they will try on Monday.

evidence.claim: Learning environments can take enrolments, collect feedback and generate certificates from attendance.

assumptions: Boundary: from the school request to certificates issued; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: library kept by the lecturer; fallback is e-mail and paper.
Schools book on the form in about the time an e-mail took.
Teachers fill the online form in about the time paper took.
research_questions: Do feedback scores rise as seminars are refined?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the seminar library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few, very different seminars; high: many seminars on the same topics.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The lecturer keeps serving on committees, planning projects with partners, building agency relations and instructing teachers; e-mail papers, proposal writing from scratch and paper certificates shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer with more time for research and teachers.
